prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Customer Onboarding Field Validation Rules (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Field" · longest unbreakable word 126px · one-line width 126px
  col 2: header "Pattern" · longest unbreakable word 114px · one-line width 1074px
  col 3: header "Example valid" · longest unbreakable word 167px · one-line width 264px
  col 4: header "Error message" · longest unbreakable word 157px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A developer/QA reference sheet: for each onboarding form field it gives the validation regex, a valid sample, and the message shown on failure — a lookup table read row by row while implementing or testing one field.","reading":"Readers arrive knowing the field name (or scan the Field column as an index), then move right to the pattern, check it against the example, and read the error copy. Comparison happens within a row, not down a column, so each row must read as a single unit and the Field column must stay a stable anchor; the regex is the densest, most consulted content and the error text is the only true prose.","groups":["col 1 Field is the row key and stands alone — it is the lookup handle and must remain visually distinct and unbroken","col 2 Pattern + col 3 Example valid form a spec pair: the rule and a value that satisfies it, read together and verified against each other","col 4 Error message is the outcome/consequence text, the only column of ordinary prose, and can wrap freely without losing meaning"],"keep_intact":["field identifiers such as account_email, postal_code_us, currency_amount, eu_vat_id (no mid-word breaks)","regex anchors and atoms: ^, $, \\d{7,14}, [A-Za-z0-9._!...], (?:-\\d{4})? — break only at |, (, [, { boundaries, never inside a character class or quantifier","example values such as an email address or 2024-01-15 (break at @ or - at worst)"],"may_wrap":["error-message sentences — natural prose, wraps at word spaces with no loss","long regex alternation/branch sequences — wrap between groups, not inside them","header labels 'Example valid' and 'Error message' over two lines"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [147, 415, 185, 180] · table 928×849px · row heights [36, 106, 153, 106, 83, 129, 129, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 1 · OVERFLOWS the box by 568px
Design r1B: widths [147, 340, 185, 175] · table 848×919px · row heights [36, 153, 153, 106, 106, 129, 129, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 2 · OVERFLOWS the box by 488px
Design r1C: widths [147, 470, 188, 180] · table 986×849px · row heights [36, 106, 153, 106, 83, 129, 129, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 626px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"Field column sits at its 147px minimum so every identifier (account_email, postal_code_us) stays on one unbroken line and acts as a reliable row anchor. The Pattern column at 415px is wide enough that most regexes land in 3–4 lines, so the row rhythm is fairly even and the alternation groups in the email rule mostly hold together.","problems":"The email regex suffers one mid-word split: a character class / quantifier region is cut across lines, so a reader copying the pattern can no longer tell whether the break is part of the rule. Example valid (185px) and Error message (180px) are far below their one-line widths (264 / 700), so the spec pair would wrap into 2–3 lines each and the error copy into 5+ lines, inflating rows that are currently only tall because of Pattern. Row heights jump 106 → 153 → 83, which breaks vertical rhythm and makes the table look ragged. And despite all that compression the table still overflows by 568px, so the reader pays the full cost of horizontal scrolling without getting an intact regex.","cause":"Pattern 415px is just under the width the long alternation groups need (r1C shows 470px clears the splits), while Example 185 and Error 180 are squeezed to near their minimum unbreakable widths — the budget was spent on a still-inadequate Pattern and starved the two right-hand columns."},{"design":"r1B","good":"The narrowest total (848px) of the three, so the least horizontal scrolling, and the Field column is again exactly at its unbreakable minimum. Every row starts cleanly with an intact identifier, so the lookup handle survives even in a squeezed layout.","problems":"Worst regex rendering of the set: the email pattern fragments into six lines with two mid-word splits, cutting through braces and parenthesised groups so the rule becomes unreadable and un-copyable. Rows inflate to 153px and the table grows to 919px tall — taller than both wider designs — so the narrower table actually costs more vertical scrolling. The 340px Pattern is visibly cramped next to the 185px Example, an inversion of importance.","cause":"Pattern 340px is below the width needed to break only at | ( [ { boundaries; the reader loses on both axes at once — no width saving in height, and splits on top of it."},{"design":"r1C","good":"The only design with zero mid-word splits: at 470px the email regex breaks cleanly between alternation branches and character-class groups, so patterns remain legible and safe to copy. Field stays intact at 147px, and the Pattern column finally carries its weight as the densest, most-consulted content.","problems":"It is the widest table (986px, 626px overflow) and the extra width buys nothing on the right: Example valid at 188px is exactly its 167px longest-word minimum, so sample values still wrap to two lines and the 'rule + valid sample' pair can never be read on one line together. Error message at 180px wraps the prose into four-plus lines. Rows stay 106–153px tall because the regex still needs 5–6 lines, so the table is simultaneously very wide and very tall.","cause":"Pattern 470 was set by the split threshold and everything else was fitted to the leftover budget; Example and Error are under-allocated relative to their content, so width is spent where it already works and withheld where cells are actually breaking."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"regex-first","widths":[147,560,188,190],"change":"Invest almost all the added width in Pattern (470 → 560), since it is the column that determines row height and the only one whose content can be corrupted by breaking. Total 1085px: more horizontal scrolling, accepted deliberately because a reader in a 360px viewport only ever sees Field + Pattern anyway, and there the pattern should be intact and short."},{"name":"balanced-pair","widths":[147,470,215,195],"change":"Refinement of r1C, the best of the current three: keep Pattern at 470 where mid-word splits vanish, and move the freed width into Example valid (188 → 215) so the valid sample sits on one line next to its rule and the spec pair reads as a unit, with Error message at 195 so prose wraps at natural word spaces in fewer lines. Total 1027px — only ~40px wider than r1C but with the right-hand columns finally doing their job instead of being trimmed to their unbreakable minimums."},{"name":"compact-scroll","widths":[147,430,188,180],"change":"Explores the opposite trade-off for readers who cannot tolerate a 1000px scroll: pull Pattern back to 430 (the smallest width likely to still break only at alternation boundaries) and keep Example 188 / Error 180 at their minimums, for a 945px table — about 40px narrower than r1C and over 100px narrower than the two above. Accepts a small risk of one mid-word split in the email rule in exchange for a table the reader can traverse with noticeably less horizontal travel, testing whether split-free regexes are worth the extra scroll."}]}
